axes.question: Which project layer does this section mainly describe?

interface.what: Caller-facing surface: CLI commands, flags, HTTP routes, or public APIs.
interface.not_for: Internal module boundaries (platform), domain vocabulary, or operator runbooks.
examples: seed --dry-run must not retain.
orto mental-model propose prints catalog proposals.

domain.what: Product or domain vocabulary, invariants, and business rules.
domain.not_for: CLI contracts (interface), Docker ops (ops), or repo coding standards (docs).
examples: Bank id is not the Docker container name.
Durable knowledge outlives a single agent session.

platform.what: Internal architecture: modules, boundaries, and where a concern lives.
platform.not_for: Public CLI flags (interface), or how an operator upgrades Docker (ops).
examples: Scanner, extractor, and seeder stay separate.
Commands must not own extraction.

ops.what: Operator runbooks: install, upgrade, auth, recovery, and deployment profiles.
ops.not_for: Module ownership (platform), or contributor coding conventions (docs).
examples: docker upgrade plans a pinned image move.
ORTO_HINDSIGHT_API_KEY is required for tenant auth.

docs.what: Contributor process, coding standards, and how the repo is documented.
examples: Prefer small, focused changes.
Throw OrtoError and name the next step.

axes.question: Which product domain does this section belong to?

product.what: Core product purpose and user-facing capabilities.
product.not_for: Engineering process, security policy, or generic other topics.
examples: Orto turns durable project knowledge into Hindsight banks.
Company brain config for AI agents.

engineering.what: How the software is built: TypeScript, tests, module layout, extraction.
engineering.not_for: Security/auth policy (security), or release/ops process alone (process).
examples: Vitest covers judge and seeder domain logic.
Strict TypeScript; avoid any.

process.what: Team process: release, review, roadmap, and contribution workflow.
examples: Update ROADMAP.md when a phase item ships.
Prefer --dry-run on mutating commands.

security.what: Secrets, credentials, auth, and sensitive-data rules.
security.not_for: General coding style (engineering), or product mission (product).
examples: Never retain .env or credential paths.
API keys stay in the environment, not config.json.

other.what: Durable knowledge that does not fit product, engineering, process, or security.
other.not_for: Anything that clearly belongs in one of the other domain bins.
examples: Historical context about an archived prototype.
A cross-cutting note with no single owner domain.

axes.question: How stable is this claim for agents?

frozen.what: A settled constraint or decision that should not drift without an explicit ADR.
frozen.not_for: Guidance that is expected to evolve as the product changes.
examples: Local-first is a non-negotiable default.
document_id stays orto:<path>#<section>.

evolving.what: True today but expected to change as the product or process matures.
evolving.not_for: Constitutional invariants that must stay frozen.
examples: Default Hindsight image tag in docker up.
Starter mental-model catalog contents.
